subject: Token velocity forecast & GPU runway — Oakstream deal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <pri.shah@oakstream.ai>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@oakstream.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token velocity forecast & GPU runway — Oakstream deal

Hi Priyanka / Aaron —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As requested, I started a quick thread to collect the traffic samples and propose a first-pass token-velocity -> GPU runway estimate so your procurement team has something to react to this week.

What we need from you to lock a committed pool recommendation:
- Typical model(s) you plan to run (and whether you prefer a quantized variant)
- Distribution: avg tokens per request, 95th/99th percentile request sizes, and peak concurrent requests by time of day
- Target latency SLO (p95 or p99) and acceptable p99 tail (e.g., p95 < 250ms, p99 < 600ms)
- Any hard blackout windows or bursty ingest patterns (calendar-based)

Based on the high-level signals you mentioned on the call (mix of instruction-following LMs, heavy morning spikes), I can give a preliminary banded sizing:
- Baseline: 1,500 tokens/sec sustained (approx. 1 model-optimized GPU)
- Spike capacity: 6,000 tokens/sec peak (approx. 3-4 GPUs to maintain p95 latency targets with 20% headroom)

These are rough until we see your sample. If you can drop a small CSV of a day's traffic (timestamps, request_tokens) and confirm the target model, Marissa will run a short runbook and turn around a slab recommendation (committed tier + suggested burst buffer).

I'm including Marissa + Ben on this thread for the sizing math and procurement playbook. Would you be available for a 30-minute sizing call Thursday 4/22 at 9am PT?

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: oak_traffic_sample.csv (CSV stub, 120KB)

From: Priyanka Shah <pri.shah@oakstream.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@oakstream.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token velocity forecast & GPU runway — Oakstream deal

Thanks Jordan —

Attached is a 48-hour sample and a short note on our traffic. Key points:
- Models: production uses Redwood-optimized-Large (comparable to 34B) for core recommendations; we plan a fallback to medium quantized 8-bit model for cost bursts.
- Avg tokens per request: 120 tokens (median), 95th: 640 tokens, 99th: 1,900 tokens
- Typical steady state: ~1,200 tokens/sec between 11am–4pm PT.
- Morning burst: 7:30–9:00am PT daily with sustained peaks up to 5,500 tokens/sec for 10–20 minute windows.
- SLA aspiration: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 800ms for online recommendations.
- Procurement timeline: aiming for committed pool sign-off by end of May; we'd like three sized options (conservative, target, and aggressive).

I attached the CSV (oak_traffic_sample.csv) and our procurement timeline doc. Let us know if you want a full 7-day sample — we can provide it but wanted to start small.

Priyanka Shah
Head of Product, Oakstream Labs
---
Attachment: oak_traffic_sample.csv (CSV stub, 1.1MB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyanka Shah <pri.shah@oakstream.ai>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@oakstream.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token velocity forecast & GPU runway — Oakstream deal

Jordan / Priyanka —

I ran the 48-hour sample through our quick simulator and produced a compact runway spreadsheet (attached: oakstream_runway_calc.xlsx). Notes / assumptions up-front:
- Model perf: Redwood-optimized-Large = ~1,400 tokens/sec per A100s-equivalent GPU at quantization=4/8 mixed path with batching tuned for p95 latency. Fallback quantized-medium = ~4,200 tokens/sec per GPU (lower quality, smaller memory pressure).
- Average seq length used: 120 tokens; peak seq length: 1,900 tokens (we cap batch size to avoid p99 amplification).
- Target SLO interpreted as p95 < 300ms. We size to keep p95 below target with ~20% thermal headroom and 30% soft headroom for short bursts.

Summary of the three banded options (tokens/sec -> GPU equivalents):
1) Conservative (3-month safety): steady 1,200 tps baseline, peak 5,500 tps -> allocate 6 GPUs (baseline 1.2k mapped to 1 GPU each but account for concurrency; peak headroom to 6 GPUs)
2) Target (expected): steady 1,500 tps, peak 5,500 tps -> allocate 5 GPUs (1.5k per GPU assumption for mixed load, 2x burstable credit)
3) Aggressive (growth-ready): steady 3,000 tps, peak 7,000 tps -> allocate 9 GPUs (mix of dedicated + autoscale to burst pool)

Specifics in the sheet: token/sec -> GPU mapping, expected p95 latency contours, cost buckets (monthly committed vs burst-overage). I also added a sensitivity tab that shows p95 latency degradation if average tokens/request increases by 30% or peak windows double.

Recommended next steps:
- Review the attached sheet; confirm whether the fallback quantized-medium is acceptable for spill traffic (it reduces cost but adds regressive quality risk).
- If procurement prefers a conservative commit, we'll draft a 6-GPU monthly slab with a 25% burst buffer (DocuSign estimate attached).

On the technical side, Ben can prepare a short runbook for cache priming and prefix caching to reduce steady-state tokens/sec by up to 12% for repeated session patterns.

Marissa Cole
Principal, Inference Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: oakstream_runway_calc.xlsx (XLSX stub, 420KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <pri.shah@oakstream.ai>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@oakstream.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token velocity forecast & GPU runway — Oakstream deal

Thanks Marissa / Priyanka —

This is great—Marissa's banding gives procurement the three clean options we discussed. A couple of operational points to surface to Oakstream procurement and platform:
- Autoscale policy: recommend "dedicated base" (6 GPUs conservative) + burst pool (3 GPUs shared across region) with automatic fallback to quantized-medium for overflow. We can set burst thresholds by token/sec and by sustained window (e.g., only trigger when >2 minutes).
- Canary/fallback: we'll pin the model version for the canary and set a 10% traffic canary for the first week after rollout, with automatic rollback on quality regressions flagged by your eval set.
- Cost optimization: enable prefix caching for repeated sessions and aggressive batching on long-tail requests during off-peak (we'll provide parameter presets).

Can we lock a 30-minute working session Wed 4/28 10:00am PT to go through the sheet and finalize the DocuSign estimate? I'm sending the DocuSign draft to you now (attached: oakstream_docusign_estimate.pdf).

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: oakstream_docusign_estimate.pdf (PDF stub, 58KB)

From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@oakstream.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token velocity forecast & GPU runway — Oakstream deal

Jordan / Marissa / Team —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Procurement reviewed the three options and prefers to proceed with the Target band (5 GPUs) with a 30-day buffer on add/remove timing. A couple requests before sign-off:
- Can you add a short paragraph in the DocuSign estimate that clarifies the burst buffer billing model and how overage invoices are computed?
- Please confirm expected p95 latency at 5 GPUs for the Redwood-optimized-Large profile in the spreadsheet (we want the numeric contour in the DocuSign exhibit).

If you can add those two items, procurement is comfortable moving to internal approvals this week and we'll aim to hit end-of-May for the commitment.

Thanks,
Aaron Liu
VP Engineering, Oakstream Labs
